queries.heading: What is CagriSema?
queries.answer: CagriSema is a fixed-dose combination of two once-weekly injectable drugs from Novo Nordisk: cagrilintide, a long-acting amylin analogue that is still investigational, and semaglutide, the approved GLP-1 drug sold as Ozempic and Wegovy. Both are given at 2.4 mg in one injection. It has been through a large phase 3 programme for weight management and type 2 diabetes and is not approved in any country.

CagriSema against tirzepatide: the head-to-head trial that missed its endpoint
queries.boundary: One head-to-head trial exists and it is the one people do not quote. In February 2026 the company announced that CagriSema reached 23% weight loss over 84 weeks but did not show non-inferiority to tirzepatide 15 mg, its primary endpoint.

queries.heading: Side effects, measured against the components and against placebo
queries.boundary: Gastrointestinal effects dominate, as with every drug in this class. In the largest diabetes trial 86.9% of the combination group reported an adverse event against 81.2% on semaglutide alone and 70.5% on placebo.

queries.heading: What about muscle loss on CagriSema?
queries.answer: The trials reported weight, blood sugar, waist circumference and blood pressure. Body composition was measured in substudies, including an MRI substudy in one of the diabetes trials, and those results are not in the abstracts this page quotes. As with any rapid weight loss, part of what is lost is lean tissue; no published figure separates that for this combination.

queries.heading: How is CagriSema different from Ozempic?
queries.answer: Ozempic is semaglutide alone, at doses up to 2 mg for type 2 diabetes. CagriSema is semaglutide 2.4 mg plus cagrilintide 2.4 mg in one weekly injection. The added drug is an amylin analogue, which works on a different satiety pathway, and in the largest trial the combination produced roughly a third more weight loss than semaglutide alone.

queries.heading: Is CagriSema the same as tirzepatide?
queries.answer: No. Tirzepatide is a single molecule that activates the GLP-1 and GIP receptors, made by Eli Lilly. CagriSema is two molecules in one injection, semaglutide for GLP-1 and cagrilintide for the amylin receptors, made by Novo Nordisk. They were compared directly in one trial, which CagriSema did not win.

information_gain: The only page that treats this as a combination question and answers it with the trial arms that exist: in the largest trial the combination reached 22.7% weight loss against 16.1% for semaglutide alone, 11.8% for cagrilintide alone and 2.3% for placebo, so the benefit of combining is measurable and smaller than the headline. The only page to explain why the same trial is quoted as 20.4% in the New England Journal and as 22.7% by the manufacturer, which is the estimand difference and the source of most of the disagreement online. The only page to put the head-to-head trial against tirzepatide in its place: 23% weight loss over 84 weeks, and a failure to show non-inferiority, which is the result the comparison pages leave out. And the only page to note what CagriSema is not: a stack anyone can assemble, since it is a fixed-dose product that does not exist outside the trials.
serp_format_rewarded: Primary literature and regulatory status. The SERP is PubMed, the Lancet, the manufacturer and a drug database; there is no dosing guide to displace and the incumbent has nothing. A trial table with the component arms, an estimand explanation and a plain status statement fits what is already ranking and answers what those pages do not.
